title: Private VPC Deploy Safety Contract: No-Egress (air-gapped) Upgrade & Network Acceptance Criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines the product acceptance criteria and operational contract for Private/VPC customer sites that operate in strict no-egress (air-gapped or limited-egress) mode. It captures networking preconditions, upgrade artifact distribution patterns, operator safety requirements, validation gates, and measurable success criteria so that Sales/Support/Onboarding teams can sign customer commitments. The goal is to provide a deterministic, auditable upgrade and bootstrap path that requires zero outbound connectivity to public endpoints while preserving rollback safety and minimal manual operator effort.
acceptance_criteria: Network prerequisites documented and verifiable: site MTU, TCP window settings, DNS split-horizon behavior, required ports between operator control plane and node agents, and expected route tables must be enumerated and testable by devops teams.

Upgrade artifact delivery modes supported: (a) signed tar bundle via secure file transfer, (b) mirrored private repository (HTTPS) hosted inside the VPC, and (c) physical media ingestion. Each mode must include signature verification and provenance metadata.
Operator validates artifact signatures and checks image provenance prior to install; any mismatch rejects the upgrade and emits a labeled incident event.

Zero-external-egress upgrade end-to-end flow: from artifact staging to canary application, health verification, and full rollout where no component initiates outbound HTTPS to public hosts during the process.

Staged canary: upgrades must support a 2-stage rollout by default (node-group canary then cluster-wide), with automatic halt on specified telemetry regressions and manual-continue guardrails in the Console.

Automated rollback: when canary fails predefined health checks or SLO regressions exceed thresholds, system must auto-revert to the prior image within the same maintenance window and report root cause markers.
Maintenance window contract: operator supports scheduled quiesce, per-cluster quiesce indicators, and operator-driven draining with idempotent resume semantics after restart.

Telemetry and degraded-mode observability must function offline: local metrics collectors must retain 30 days of telemetry and provide export helpers for periodic pull or bundle collection without requiring outbound telemetry upload.
KMS and secret rotation: support for customer-managed KMS keys (HSM/KMS) that can be rotated offline; operator must accept key bundles and apply rotations without contacting external KMS endpoints.
Upgrade verification duration: end-to-end artifact validation and preflight checks must complete within 10 minutes on target hardware profiles or provide deterministic failure reasons.

Compatibility gating: operator prevents upgrades when incompatible kernel modules, unsupported MTU, or missing firewall rules are detected; explicit overrides require documented risk acceptance by on-call and customer security contact.
Compatibility matrix: documented minimum OS/container runtime versions and permissive kernel flags must be included and validated by preflight checks.
Audit trail: every upgrade action (stage, approve, reject, rollback) must be recorded with immutable signed logs accessible to customer auditors.
No silent fallback to hosted services: in no-egress mode the system must not attempt to use hosted fallbacks; warnings and explicit failover procedures must be surfaced to the operator instead.

Operator performance guardrails: CPU/memory thresholds for operator pods and upgrade controller must be defined to avoid overload during bulk package application, with backoff strategies to prevent cascading failures.
operational_checklist: Preflight network test script (available in repo) executed and green: DNS resolution, MTU verification, port connectivity matrix.
Signed artifact generated and its SHA512 published in a sidecar manifest stored inside the customer's mirror or physical media.
On-prem mirror health check (if used): TLS certs valid, repo index consistent, and GC disabled for rollout period.
Operator safe-mode toggle exists and is documented; on toggle, automatic rollouts are paused and only manual approval is accepted.
Backup snapshot created before upgrade and retention tag applied for 7 days minimum.
On-call and customer security contact scheduled for the maintenance window; rollback playbook reviewed.
Local telemetry bundling procedure executed and sample artifact captured for later forensic analysis.
test_scenarios: Offline upgrade via signed tar bundle transferred by SFTP: validate signature, apply upgrade, run smoke tests, and assert zero external DNS/HTTP traffic.
Mirror-based upgrade over private HTTPS with deliberately throttled bandwidth to emulate constrained on-prem links; ensure timeout/backoff behaviors are correct.
Canary failure injection: introduce latency or pod restart during canary and assert automatic halt + rollback occurs and logs are emitted.
KMS key rotation using supplied key bundle without outbound KMS calls and validate encrypted secrets remain readable post-rotation.
Operator restart during upgrade: simulate operator process restart to validate idempotence and resume semantics.
Image provenance tampering: change manifest signature and assert the operator rejects the artifact with an auditable error.
rollback_plan: Automated rollback to previous image on health-check failure with a rollback window target of <=15 minutes.
Manual rollback path documented with CLI steps and Console 'revert' button for operator-run remediation.
Rollback verification suite (subset of smoke tests) executed automatically post-rollback and reported to on-call channel.
If rollback fails, operator escalates to Escalation: contact engineering on-call and follow offline emergency patch protocol.
For physical media deployments, maintain a secondary verified media image to expedite reinstallation if in-place rollback is unrecoverable.
observability_requirements: Local metrics retention of 30 days and ability to export compressed bundles for out-of-band analysis.
Health endpoints for each subcomponent that return structured status codes suitable for automated gating (OK / DEGRADED / FAIL).
Preflight and postflight upgrade reports stored in the cluster and annotated with artifact SHA and operator identity.
Audit logs signed and checksummed; retention policy of 365 days configurable by customer.
Console must present a clear upgrade timeline with per-node status and human-readable failure reasons for the first failed check.
success_metrics: Upgrade success rate in no-egress mode >= 99% across pilot customers for first 3 months.
Median time-to-validate artifact signatures <= 30 seconds on supported hardware.
Mean time-to-rollback after failure <= 15 minutes for automated rollback scenarios.
< 2 customer-visible incidents attributable to upgrade mechanism across the first 10 production rollouts.
Customer onboarding checklist completion time reduced by 25% after publishing preflight tooling and docs.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Hidden network middleboxes rewrite headers causing TLS/mirror failure. Mitigation: include packet-capture preflight with pattern checks and an explicit 'unsupported network device' flag.
Risk: Operator overload during large-scale patching. Mitigation: rate limiting and jittered, prioritized rollout by zone.
Risk: Human error when using physical media. Mitigation: signed manifests, step-by-step playbook, and checksum validation tools.
Risk: Telemetry unavailability hampers root cause analysis. Mitigation: local retention + retrieval playbooks and sample retention policy.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids prescribing a single distribution mechanism; supporting multiple artifact delivery modes is required to meet diverse customer environments.
We will run a 6-customer pilot to validate the no-egress upgrade flows before including this as a standard offering in the private product tier.
Coordinate with Security to finalize audit log signing scheme and with Eng Infra for tooling to create signed offline bundles.
Design should include a lightweight UI for operators to inspect preflight artifacts and to drill into failed checks with remediation hints.
communication_plan: Pre-pilot announcement to selected pilot customers with checklist and support hours.
Internal runbook and Slack channel #private-upgrades for pilot duration.
Post-pilot feedback session and sign-off before GA.
Documentation update in customer onboarding portal and release notes.
